statement: For iid compactly supported real V on Z^d, d>=1, and any fixed m in supp(mu), almost surely arbitrarily distant L-cubes with every |V_x-m|<1/L exist for every integer L. Their normalized cutoff plane waves give, simultaneously for every E in [-2d,2d], ||(H0-E)psi_L||<=2d sqrt(2/L) and ||(V-m)psi_L||<=1/L.
proof: Independent disjoint cube trials have fixed positive success probability for each L; countable intersection and explicit cutoff shift defects.
remaining_gap: No gap in the author proof; independent checking pending. This is not a spectral-type statement.
scope: auxiliary lemma; parent target not solved

statement: For bounded iid real V with M=ess sup |V_x|>0 on Z^d, almost surely simultaneously for all E in [-2d,2d], eta>0, lambda>0 and integers n>=0, with R0=(H0-E-i eta)^(-1) and K=lambda V R0, ||K^n||=(lambda M/eta)^n, r(K)=lambda M/eta, and ||R0 K^n||=eta^(-1)(lambda M/eta)^n. The unrenormalized Born resolvent series converges in operator norm if and only if eta>lambda M.
proof: L1 cubes near an extremal support point supply common approximate eigenvectors for R0 and K. Exact telescoping power bounds establish necessity, including eta=lambda M; the norm geometric series establishes sufficiency.
remaining_gap: Independent checking pending. Original fixed-disorder a.c. spectral mass and GOE statistics remain unproved.
scope: sharp route obstruction; not a refutation of C0056

statement: Under L2's hypotheses with centered site law, E[K]=0 weakly, but E[||R0 K^n||]=eta^(-1)(lambda M/eta)^n. Centering alone therefore cannot yield disorder-averaged operator-norm convergence of the unrenormalized Born series below its exact threshold.
proof: Centering gives the weak operator expectation; the norm identity holds almost surely and is deterministic, so its expectation is unchanged.
remaining_gap: Independent checking pending; does not address averaged entries or renormalized methods.
